info.title: Pumasi dashboard API
info.description: Served by `pumasi ui`. Every call is made with the caller's Pumasi ticket (admin, submitter or viewer), whose role the control plane enforces. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <ticket>` (a `pumasiadmin...` admin or access ticket), or with a signed-in browser session plus the `X-Pumasi-CSRF` header on POST. Job ids are hex strings; CU amounts are integers in milli-CU, rates in micro-CU. With `pumasi ui --api-only` only bearer tickets are taken. After 10 failed sign-ins or wrong tickets within a minute, a client address gets 429 for 5 minutes. Each ticket may make 120 requests in a burst and 20 a second after that (429 with Retry-After beyond), and hold at most 8 `?wait=` requests open at once. Request bodies are limited to 1 MiB, except job submissions (the upload limit) and `/api/v1/op` (32 MiB).

get.summary: This document
The ticket's name, role and job policy
get.description: For a submitter ticket, `account`, `policy`, `quota` and `usage` say what its jobs may ask for and how much is in use; for other roles they are `null`.

get.summary: Cluster status: nodes and jobs
get.description: Submitters see only their account's jobs. Each node carries `power` (1.5; missing when the control plane is older): `asleep_since_unix` while the machine is asleep after saying so, `report` (what its agent does about sleep: `stays_awake`, `sleep_notice`, `wake_on_lan`, `on_pause`, and its LAN network cards in `lan`), `last_wake_unix` and `last_wake_by` for the last magic packet, and `can_wake` (some machine of the cluster is online on its LAN).

get.summary: Node metrics and cluster counters
get.description: Every node's latest sample; with `node`, its time series over `since` seconds (step_secs: 10 up to 1 h, 60 up to 24 h, 600 beyond).

get.summary: Cluster events, oldest first
get.description: Cursor-based: pass the last `seq` you saw as `after`. With `after` 0, the newest `limit`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Not older than this Unix time

get.summary: Alert rules, firing alerts and webhooks
get.description: Since 1.6 also `tuning` (`repeat_secs`: send a firing alert's notice again this often, `resolved`: send a notice when it stops, `overrides`: other `node_offline_secs`, `disk_percent` and `temp_c` for the nodes a selector picks), `silences` (rule, nodes, `until_unix`, comment, who) and `silenced` (firing alerts a silence keeps quiet, as [rule, subject]). They are missing when the control plane is older.

post.summary: Silence alerts for a while: no webhook notices for them (1.6, admin)

rule.description: node_offline, failure_rate, disk, temperature, perf_drop, smart or check_mismatch; missing: every rule

on.description: A node name or a label selector (`os=windows`); missing: every node and the cluster

for.description: How long, e.g. `2h` (default), at most 90 days

delete.summary: End a silence (id or unique prefix; 1.6, admin)

post.summary: Send a test alert to a webhook now and wait for its answer (1.6, admin)

get.summary: Round trips and bandwidth the nodes measured between each other (1.6)
get.description: `nodes` (names), `links` (`from`, `to`, `rtt_us`, `bps` in bytes per second, `direct`, `unix`, `error`) and `every_secs` (how often the control plane asks for a probe, 0: never).

200.description: With `validate`: the job would be accepted

post.description: Same as `pumasi run`: a job.toml (field `job`, or a file named job.toml) and the files it names (fields `files`, with relative paths as file names). Large shared inputs go through the file store. With `?validate=1` nothing is submitted: the job goes through the same checks (the ticket's role, the account's policy and quotas, the job's files) and the answer is 200, or the error a real submission would get.

after.description: Job ids that must succeed first, comma separated

parameters.name: validate
parameters.description: Check the job without submitting it

get.summary: A job and its tasks

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id (hex, as `pumasi status` shows it)

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Long poll: wait up to this long for the job to finish (`30s`, `2m`; a bare number is seconds; at most 90s)

get.description: With `?wait=`, answers as soon as the job finishes (succeeded, failed or cancelled) or when the wait runs out, whichever comes first; check `summary.state`. Waits of more than 90s are cut to 90s, under the 100s a Cloudflare Tunnel allows. Each task carries `node_name` next to `node`, and how long it waited (`queued_ms`), fetched its inputs (`fetch_ms`), pulled its image (`pull_ms`), ran (`run_ms`) and stored its output (`upload_ms`). `wall_ms` and the receipt cover `run_ms` only.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id (hex, as `pumasi status` shows it)

get.summary: Signed usage receipts
get.description: The `pumasi receipts --export` format; `pumasi verify-receipts` checks a saved copy offline.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id (hex, as `pumasi status` shows it)

get.summary: Every task's output files as a zip
get.description: Inline outputs and outputs kept in the file store, as `task-<index>/<path>`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id (hex, as `pumasi status` shows it)

get.summary: A task's output from byte offsets
get.description: Poll with `stdout_next` and `stderr_next` as the next offsets; when `attempt` changes the task started over and offsets restart at 0. `live` is false for microVM tasks, whose output comes when they end.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Job id (hex, as `pumasi status` shows it)

post.summary: Give a node a display name, or go back to the name its agent reports
post.description: Admin only. The name (up to 64 characters, unique in the cluster) shows in the status, the dashboard, events and the built-in `name` label, and can be used wherever a node name is taken. It survives the agent restarting with another `--name`. `null`, an empty string or a missing `name` goes back to the agent's name.

post.summary: Drain, cordon, uncordon, benchmark, wake, trust or untrust a node (trust: it runs tier = "trusted" jobs; wake: send the Wake-on-LAN magic packet of an offline node that opted in, 1.5)

get.summary: The newest published release and the state of an upgrade to it
get.description: Answers `{source, latest, checked_unix, check_error, control_plane, fetch}`. `fetch` is `"Idle"`, `{"Running": {version, step, started_unix}}`, `{"Done": {version, summary, finished_unix}}` or `{"Failed": {version, reason, finished_unix}}`. With `check=true` (admin only) the control plane asks the release site first (at most once a minute); otherwise it answers with what it last saw. Where each node stands in the rollout: `POST /api/v1/op` with `"RolloutStatus"`.

post.summary: Upgrade the cluster to the newest published release (or `version`)
post.description: Admin only. The control plane downloads the binary of every platform its nodes run, checks each against the release's SHA256SUMS, its platform and its build marker, and rolls them out like `pumasi upgrade rollout` (signed with the cluster key; nodes install when idle and roll back on failure). Answers at once with the same view as `GET`; poll it until `fetch` is `Done` or `Failed`. Nodes already on that version or newer are left alone.

version.description: A release tag such as v1.3.0 (default: the newest release)

force.description: Allow binaries of another protocol version than the control plane

get.summary: Account balances (milli-CU)
An account's job policy, quota and use
get.description: Admins and viewers may read any account, a submitter only its own. 404 when the account has no quota, policy or jobs.

patch.summary: Change an account's job policy or quota
patch.description: Admin only. Changes only the fields in the body and answers the result. A list takes the whole list or `{"add": [...], "remove": [...]}`, so adding one image needs no read first. Removing the last entry of `images` or `executors` is refused, because an empty list allows everything; send `[]` to mean that. What GET answers can be sent back as it is.

get.summary: Ledger entries, newest first
Datasets: the latest version of each, or every version of `name`
Store usage per account and quotas
CU rates and settlement policy (micro-CU rates)
TEE nodes, trusted hosts and the launch measurements seen (confidential tier); trust one with the TrustMeasurement op

post.summary: Create a join ticket or a provider invite
post.description: Without `account`: a ticket for the owner's own machines (default 24 h). With it: an invite for someone else's machine earning for that account (default 7 days).
The JSON form of the protocol's `AdminOp`, e.g. `"Status"` or `{"Drain": {"node": "mac-mini"}}`; the answer is the matching `AdminResponse`. The control plane checks the ticket's role as for the CLI.

get.summary: Audit log entries (admin tickets only), oldest first
get.description: Who changed what: every call that changes the cluster, refused calls, sign-ins and nodes joining. Each entry carries `prev` and `hash` (hex BLAKE3) forming a chain. Cursor-based: pass the last `seq` you saw as `after`; with `after` 0, the newest `limit`.

get.summary: Checks the whole audit chain and returns its head, signed by the cluster key (admin tickets only)
get.description: `signature` is Ed25519 by the cluster key (`cluster`, an iroh endpoint id) over `pumasi/audit-head/v1\0 || seq (u64 LE) || hash || unix (u64 LE)`. Keep a head elsewhere and compare later: `pumasi audit verify --against`.

ticket.description: A Pumasi admin or access ticket

Error.description: The call failed; the message says why (e.g. the ticket's role does not allow it)

images.description: Image patterns a job may name (`ghcr.io/lab/*`); empty allows any image

require_digest.description: Images must be pinned by digest

executors.description: Executors a job may use; empty allows all

network.description: `deny` refuses jobs that ask for network access

selector.description: Node selector added to every job (`zone=lab,gpu`); empty for none

tolerations.description: Taints a job may tolerate; `null` allows any, an empty list none

max_timeout_ms.description: Longest task timeout; `null` for no limit

max_gpus_per_task.description: Most GPUs one task may ask for; `null` for no limit

cu_per_day.description: Spending per day, in thousandths of a CU

spent_day.description: Spent in the last day, in thousandths of a CU

AccountPolicyView.description: An account's job policy, with its name, quota and current use

ListChange.description: A list (replaces the whole list), or what to add to and remove from the current one. Adding an entry that is there and removing one that is not change nothing.

AccountPolicyPatch.description: Only the fields that are given change. `null` lifts a limit. Unknown fields are refused.

require_digest.description: Images must be pinned by digest

network.description: `deny` refuses jobs that ask for network access

selector.description: Node selector added to every job (`zone=lab,gpu`); empty for none

tolerations.description: `null` allows any taint; otherwise a list or a change to it

max_timeout_ms.description: Longest task timeout; `null` for no limit

max_gpus_per_task.description: Most GPUs one task may ask for; `null` for no limit

account.description: If given, must be the account in the path

usage.description: Ignored, so that what GET answers can be sent back

account.description: The account the job would be billed to

ready_nodes.description: Names of the nodes that would start one of its tasks right now

waiting.description: Why no task would start right now (jobs it waits for, the account's quota, or each node with its reason); `null` when a node is ready

Task.description: One task of a job. The times are omitted when the control plane is older than 1.4; agents older than 1.4 report no `fetch_ms`, `pull_ms` or `upload_ms` (they read 0).

node.description: Id of the node the task ran on

node_name.description: That node's name when the task was placed

wall_ms.description: Time the task itself ran, on the node's clock; the same as `run_ms`

queued_ms.description: Time the run that counted waited in the queue for a node (since the job was submitted, its dependencies finished, or the run before it failed)

fetch_ms.description: Time on the node fetching what the task mounts from the cluster's file store (datasets, large inputs, a private image)

pull_ms.description: Time pulling the image; 0 when the node already had it

run_ms.description: Time the task itself ran. This is `wall_ms`, and the only time the receipt bills.

upload_ms.description: Time storing the task's output in the file store; 0 when the output went with the result

ran_as.description: The executor the task's latest run used: for an `executor = "image"` job, `docker` or `microvm` (1.5). Null before the task is placed; omitted when the control plane is older than 1.5
